title.narrative: URGENT EARLY RECOVERY AND RESILIENCE BUILDING TOWARDS RECONSTRUCTION IN THE GAZA STRIP

description.narrative: The Gaza Strip has endured multiple military escalations since the imposed blockade in 2007 (2008–2009, 2012, 2014, 2021, and now) resulting in catastrophic humanitarian impacts on Palestinian civilians. The impact of the current ongoing war far exceeds those during previous escalations that have profoundly impacted the Gaza Strip. The current war is the most destructive, brutal, and damaging to the Strip, that spares no civilians, residential areas, infrastructure, public buildings and public services, including schools, hospitals, universities, electricity and water stations, sewage networks, as well as cultural and religious buildings, among others. The ongoing crises in Gaza Strip have significantly impacted the lives of vulnerable communities, exacerbated the socio-economic challenges and created a dire need for immediate response and sustainable interventions. The proposed project aims to Provide humanitarian assistance and critical support to crisis affected population in Gaza Strip by alleviating suffering, restoring essential services, and ensuring immediate access to emergency relief and shelter. This project aims to aid the displaced and vulnerable populations and facilitate urgent recovery efforts, while creating pathways out of the ongoing acute humanitarian crisis and establishing the foundation for rebuilding in a more resilient and sustainable manner.The proposed project aligns with the State of Palestine’s “Gaza Relief and Early Recovery Plan”, which integrates humanitarian assistance with emergency recovery efforts. The plan’s Comprehensive Response Program (implemented during 6-18 months post ceasefire) includes “building transitional prefabricated buildings for housing close to the neighborhoods to be reconstructed, with the basic services of health, education, water, wastewater, energy, and solid waste management are provided, in addition to providing other essential governmental and municipal services”. It emphasizes the urgent need to reactivate essential services by repairing infrastructure, reconnecting water and sanitation systems, energy, and telecommunications networks, and enabling government agencies to swiftly resume operations . Moreover, the Gaza Strip Interim Damage Assessment, highlighted that “While recovery and reconstruction will require substantial, years-long effort, early recovery actions should begin as soon as the situation allows, and complement scaled up humanitarian assistance. Priority early recovery actions that should be considered include enabling access to, and the resumption of, essential health and education services, to reestablish a sense of normalcy and provide direly needed psychosocial support. The provision of shelter and rapid, cost-effective, and scalable rehousing solutions for displaced people, combined with the resumption of basic services in energy, water and telecom sectors should also be prioritized . Additionally, in its Programme Criticality Framework for the oPt, developed as part of the response to the ongoing crisis, the UNCT in Palestine has highlighted a list of urgent priority interventions, including: (i) Operate, rehabilitate and repair damaged infrastructure and assets for basic services and livelihoods, (ii) Support community awareness raising on mine action, housing, land, and property rights, preventative health measures, non-communicable diseases, healthy lifestyles and conduct mental health and psychosocial wellbeing, (iii) Provide self-help construction for reconstructions, repairs and/or improvements of housing and essential livelihood assets (including in refugee camps) . International experiences and studies in this field have proven that early planning for reconstruction is essential , as it allows for the immediate start of rebuilding essential infrastructure such as roads, schools, hospitals, and homes, which are critical for long-term development. Moreover, early recovery plans often include strategies to revive local economies by restoring markets, creating jobs, and supporting small businesses, laying the groundwork for sustainable economic growth. A well-structured early recovery plan can attract international support and funding, as donors are more inclined to invest in organized recovery efforts with clear goals and strategies. This enhances the scalability of the intervention. Similarly, best practices have shown that the following principles should be considered when recovery plans are developed: (i) balancing urgent needs with medium- and long-term goals, (ii) ensuring an approach of building back better and more resiliently, (iii) targeting the most vulnerable, and (iv) ensuring inclusive and participatory planning through a whole-of-community approach . The proposed project builds on these principles and intends to adopt an inclusive participatory planning approach that engages vulnerable communities and contributes to restoring the livability of the targeted areas.
